words.engDef: to bring to an end; close or cancel a formal agreement
words.example: The corporation decided to terminate the contract due to poor vendor performance.

words.engDef: to bind or compel someone legally or morally to do something
words.example: The agreement obligates both parties to maintain strict confidentiality.

words.engDef: security or protection against a loss or other financial burden
words.example: The contract includes an indemnity clause to protect the company from legal costs.

words.engDef: to compensate someone for harm or loss
words.example: The insurance policy will indemnify the homeowner against water damage.

words.engDef: of an independent body to reach an authoritative settlement in a dispute
words.example: An independent mediator was hired to arbitrate the dispute between the partners.

words.engDef: the settling of disputes by an impartial third party chosen by mutual agreement
words.example: The two parties agreed to settle their contract dispute through binding arbitration.

words.engDef: to demand or specify a requirement as part of an agreement
words.example: The lease agreement stipulates that the rent must be paid on the first of each month.

words.engDef: a condition or requirement specified as part of an agreement
words.example: One key stipulation of the merger is that no employees will be downsized.

words.engDef: a person authorized to witness signatures and certify legal documents
words.example: The signed power of attorney document must be verified by a licensed notary.

words.engDef: an agreement, contract, or written promise between two parties
words.example: The business partners signed a covenant to restrict competing operations.

words.engDef: having no force, binding power, or legal validity
words.example: If either party breaches the terms, the entire contract will become null and void.

words.engDef: a condition or qualification attached to an agreement or statement
words.example: She accepted the job offer with the proviso that she could work remotely.

words.engDef: of an agreement imposing an obligation that must be fulfilled
words.example: The written contract is a legally binding agreement between the two firms.

words.engDef: the quality of being legally binding or capable of enforcement
words.example: The company lawyer is verifying the legal enforceability of the global lease contract.

words.engDef: a person who brings a case against another in a court of law
words.example: The plaintiff claimed that the retail brand had stolen her patented design.

words.engDef: the process of taking legal action in court
words.example: Avoid costly litigation by settling the contract dispute through arbitration.

words.engDef: a writ ordering a person to attend a court as a witness
words.example: The corporate executive received a subpoena to testify during the anti-trust trial.

words.engDef: the process of giving sworn evidence out of court as part of a lawsuit
words.example: The witness gave her deposition at the lawyer's office before the trial started.

words.engDef: an authoritative warning or order by a court of law
words.example: The judge issued a preliminary injunction to stop the sale of the pirated software.

words.engDef: a written statement confirmed by oath or affirmation for use as evidence
words.example: The former employee signed an affidavit outlining corporate safety violations.

words.engDef: a party that has signed an agreement, especially a treaty or contract
words.example: The representatives of both nations are signatories to the international trade deal.

words.engDef: the state or right of owning a business or property, especially sole ownership
words.example: He decided to run his small bakery business as a sole proprietorship.

words.engDef: an authoritative order, regulation, or decree issued by local authorities
words.example: The city council passed a new ordinance restricting noise levels after midnight.

words.engDef: a person or organization that makes a formal offer for something at an auction or tender
words.example: The property was sold to the highest bidder during the competitive public auction.
